questions.question: This patient has Medicare and NY Medicaid, takes opioids regularly, and just changed Part D plans. Their 30-day refill rejects for the opioid-naïve seven-day limit. Can we bill NYRx instead, or how do we resolve the claim?
questions.answer:
For this dual-eligible patient, **do not bill NYRx to bypass the Part D reject**. NYRx says Medicaid does not cover Part D-covered drug classes for full-benefit duals and pharmacies may not circumvent Medicare billing.

Resolve through the **new Part D plan**:
1. Tell the plan/POS help desk the patient is **currently taking opioids**; CMS says the opioid-naïve 7-day hard edit can be overridden at POS by transaction code or by contacting the plan.
2. If no override, dispense up to **7 days** or have the enrollee/prescriber request a coverage determination for the full 30 days.
3. If not filled as written, give the CMS pharmacy notice.
